events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Rainier, Oregon.

evidence.quote: Miller Michael Duris was born on March 2 , 1928 , in Rainier , Oregon

events.text: Joined the United States Navy at age 17.

evidence.quote: joined the United States Navy at the age of 17 in 1945

events.text: Married Celestine Sally Weverka.

evidence.quote: the two married on October 11 , 1948

events.text: Left the United States Navy.

evidence.quote: before leaving the Navy in 1949

events.text: Began working at Tektronix as a technical writer.

evidence.quote: starting working for Tektronix in 1951

events.text: Family moved to Virginia.

evidence.quote: the family moved to Virginia in 1959

events.text: Returned to Hillsboro, Oregon.

evidence.quote: but returned to Hillsboro in 1967

events.label: founding
events.text: Started the Pigtail-Ponytail softball group for girls.

evidence.quote: He started
the Pigtail-Ponytail softball group for girls in 1969

events.text: Entered politics and was appointed to Hillsboro City Council.

evidence.quote: In 1969 , he entered politics and was appointed to the Hillsboro City Council

events.text: Re-elected to Hillsboro City Council, running unopposed.

evidence.quote: He won re-election to the council in November 1970

events.text: Began owning Millers Sweet Shop.

evidence.quote: he owned Millers Sweet Shop from 1971 to 1974

events.text: Won Hillsboro mayoral election over Kenneth Stuart.

evidence.quote: Duris then ran for mayor in 1972 , defeating Kenneth Stuart in the November election

events.text: Took office as mayor of Hillsboro.

evidence.quote: taking office on January 2 , 1973

events.text: Ended ownership of Millers Sweet Shop.

evidence.quote: he owned Millers Sweet Shop from 1971 to 1974

events.text: Re-elected mayor of Hillsboro over A. T. Antonelli.

evidence.quote: In November 1974 , he won re-election over A . T . Antonelli

events.label: legal
events.text: Land-use lawsuit reached Oregon Court of Appeals; he and co-defendants prevailed.

evidence.quote: the case reaching the Oregon Court of Appeals in 1975

events.text: Won Democratic nomination for at-large Washington County commissioner.

evidence.quote: He won the Democratic nomination over Deneice Won in the May primary

events.label: dedication
events.text: Officiated at the dedication of Bicentennial Park.

evidence.quote: he officiated at the dedication of Bicentennial Park on October 19 , 1976

events.text: Won general election for at-large Washington County commissioner.

evidence.quote: defeated Republican Allan Paterson in the general election in November

events.text: Left Tektronix.

evidence.quote: left Tektronix in 1977

events.text: Elected chairman of the Washington County Commission.

evidence.quote: On January 4 , 1978 , Duris was elected as chairman of the county commission

events.text: Won election to reconstituted county commission for a special two-year term.

evidence.quote: and then won election to the reconstituted commission in January

events.text: Ran for new at-large commissioner position in order to become chair.

evidence.quote: Duris then ran for the new at-large commissioner position in 1980 in order to be chair

events.text: No longer chairperson of the county commission.

evidence.quote: By November 1980 he was no longer the chairperson of the commission

events.text: Left office as county commissioner after losing chair race.

evidence.quote: left office in January 1981

events.text: Ran for school board of Hillsboro Union High School District; did not win.

evidence.quote: school board of the Hillsboro Union High School District ( now part of the Hillsboro School District ) in March 1986

events.text: Remained involved with the girls softball group.

evidence.quote: Duris remained involved in the group until 1988

events.text: Lost second attempt to join the same school board.

evidence.quote: in March 1988 he lost a second attempt to join the same school board

events.text: Retired from facilities manager job at Tuality Community Hospital.

evidence.quote: began working as facilities manager for Tuality Community Hospital in Hillsboro , before retiring in 1991

events.label: sports
events.text: Stopped playing in softball leagues.

evidence.quote: himself played in softball leagues until 2009

events.label: death
events.text: Died of Parkinson's disease at age 86.

evidence.quote: Duris died on March 23 , 2014 , at the age of 86 after battling Parkinsons disease
